# Plectis

> A public claim-testing layer over an AI-built system: each component names what it runs or replays, the evidence class behind it, the receipt/source handles to inspect, and the authority ceiling where the claim stops. Read order: mechanisms -> evidence discipline -> local runtime. The mechanisms are the public artifact; evidence records and local result records are the accountability layer, not the product.

Every map below is a generated projection of content-graph.json (the canonical object kernel); none of it is separately authored.

## First local command

- Source checkout: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m microcosm_core hello --reader agent .`
- Installed checkout: `plectis hello --reader agent <project>`
- First behavior card: `plectis tour --card <project>`

## Short-link first contact

If you arrived from a short link, start with the [flagship result index](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis/blob/main/FLAGSHIP_RESULTS.md). The public mathematics is a bounded result slice, not a solution to an Erdős problem: it carries two #1041 statements — finite-family translation avoidance and constant-perturbation root retention — plus a #1049 no-go for one coordinatewise clearing corridor.

That index names each source declaration, evidence scope, exact source commit, evidence pointer, and replay command. Then use the [cold-clone quickstart](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis/blob/main/QUICKSTART.md); a replay checks only the named source slice.

Scope: this is a local-first static/public project doorway. Use it to clone, inspect, and compare source-linked records; release operations, hosted service claims, external model access, source-file changes, claims not supported by the public records, formal-result correctness, production use, financial decisions, and specialist review are outside this doorway's scope.

## Repository

- Public repository (source of record): https://github.com/wcook04/plectis
- Public website (browseable wrapper over the map): https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/
- Companion Lean formalisation (eight open Erdős problems: #68, #243, #249, #251, #257, #269, #1041, #1049; all remain open, no solution claim): https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-lean-erdos249-257
- Author and purpose: built alone by a 22-year-old economics undergraduate at the University of Bristol, on a student budget, with no mathematics or computer-science training and no institutional support; the formal mathematics is entirely self-taught and the Lean work was learned for this project; Plectis and the Lean repository are the two public demonstrations of a private system (Plectis shows the machinery as runnable components, the Lean repository shows the mathematical output); the rest of that system, including its frontend and video editor, is not public
- Reading that fact correctly: it is context for calibration, not a request for allowance. The results stand or fall on the Lean source and the registry statuses either way, and should be judged there. It does mean an assumption that a corpus of this shape implies a funded team or a mathematics department is simply wrong about who built it.
- The 13 papers (PDF): erdos-68-factorial-denominator-irrationality https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/erdos-68-factorial-denominator-irrationality.pdf ; erdos-243-reciprocal-tail-rigidity https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/erdos-243-reciprocal-tail-rigidity.pdf ; erdos-249-binary-totient-series https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/erdos-249-binary-totient-series.pdf ; erdos249-totient-reasoning-surface https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/erdos249-totient-reasoning-surface.pdf ; erdos-251-prime-gap-dyadic-series https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/erdos-251-prime-gap-dyadic-series.pdf ; erdos-257-mersenne-support-subseries https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/erdos-257-mersenne-support-subseries.pdf ; erdos257-mersenne-reasoning-surface https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/erdos257-mersenne-reasoning-surface.pdf ; erdos-269-three-prime-running-lcm https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/erdos-269-three-prime-running-lcm.pdf ; erdos-1041-lemniscate-newton-flow https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/erdos-1041-lemniscate-newton-flow.pdf ; erdos-1049-rational-base-lambert https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/erdos-1049-rational-base-lambert.pdf ; claim-faithful-publication-systems https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/claim-faithful-publication-systems-paper.pdf ; cold-clone-to-proof-receipt https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/cold-clone-to-proof-receipt.pdf ; plectis-public-system https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/papers/plectis-public-system.pdf
- Strongest checked results by problem: the headline_results block inside the AI packet and reader digest carries verbatim reviewed claim statements with Lean source anchors; the Lean repository's docs/RESULTS.md is the human per-problem map. Counts are navigation scale, not results.
- Agent entry: AGENTS.md at the repository root

Objects: 781 across 16 kinds.

## The mathematics, at source

Every paper on this site ships its LaTeX beside its PDF, so the source can be read without a text-extraction pass over the typeset document and without leaving for another host. Each paper's `hosted_tex_path` is in the manifest below; hosted source mirrors each repository's own paper directory, because the two repositories carry different `paper-house-style.sty` files and a flattened copy could hold only one of them.

- [papers-source-manifest.json](papers/papers-source-manifest.json): every paper, its hosted PDF, its hosted LaTeX, and the sha256 binding each hosted copy to the public GitHub artifact it was verified against
- [claims.json](lean/claims.json): the Lean claim layer -- release identity, the status taxonomy, the remaining open propositions, the claims with their source anchors, and the explicit non-claims
- [problems.json](lean/problems.json): the per-problem index
- [RESULTS.md](lean/RESULTS.md): the per-problem map -- the strongest checked statement per problem, its exact status, and where to verify it. Hosted here as raw Markdown for offline and machine readers, on the same byte-parity terms as the two files above; it [renders on GitHub](https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-lean-erdos249-257/blob/main/docs/RESULTS.md) if you are reading it yourself
- The proofs themselves are not hosted: 1,033 Lean files, about 152 MB, plus a 72 MB per-declaration atlas. They are read by cloning https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-lean-erdos249-257, not by fetching. What is hosted here is the layer that makes a question answerable; the repository is the layer that makes it checkable.

## Reader ladder (open in order of need)

- [reader digest](plectis-ai-reader-digest.json) (~321 KB): start here -- quick_path, canonical_question_routes, headline_results, component_digest, family_digest, claim_ceiling_index, and provenance. It carries the routes and the claim ceilings without the deep bodies, which is what most questions need.
- [concise guide](assets/ai-orientation-packet.js): ~16 KB orientation for paste-only workflows -- what Plectis is, the seven areas, the rank legend.
- [AI packet](plectis-ai-review-packet.json) (~15 MB): the whole public site in one self-describing file -- read_me_first, answer contract, headline_results (the mathematics first), question routes, starter prompts, view descriptors, and every public text body. The most complete single artifact, and large enough that it is a deliberate choice rather than a default.
- [complete text corpus](plectis-ai-reader-complete.json) (~9 MB): every public text body -- all component cards, paper-module bodies, doctrine entities, glossary terms, evidence profiles, and page prose -- carried once, deduplicated, without instruction layers.
- [reference index](docs/reference.html): the human middle layer -- areas, components, doctrine records, and paper modules in one navigable roster.
- [full JSON map](plectis-site-map.json) (~18 MB): the raw map without the capsule's instruction layers -- visible_text_index bodies, page text, and diagrams, for automation.
- source of record: the public repository linked from each component's source_links.
